title: Which picture shows why up and down sums are square numbers?
description: A square grid of dots is tilted until it becomes a diamond, and its slanting rows are counted from top to bottom. The rows climb up and fall back down, which is the same as the up and down sum. Keeko doubts that a diamond can make a square number.
teaching_notes: One idea: a tilted square grid has rows that count up to the side and back down, so the up and down sum counts every dot of the square. Watch for students who think the dots of a diamond cannot be a square number.

video_script.why: The child sees why the up and down sums are square numbers, by tilting a square grid of dots and counting its slanting rows.
video_script.substitution: Use a three by three grid of dots, tilt it, count the rows, then say the same holds for a grid of any size.
video_script.anchor: a square grid of dots that is tilted into a diamond
video_script.wrong_answer: a diamond is not a square, so its dots cannot make a square number
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says a diamond is not a square, so its dots cannot make a square number. Turning the diamond back shows the same dots in a square, so the bubble is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: Rows that climb and fall in a tilted square grid add up to a square number

final_answer.value: a tilted square grid of dots has rows 1, 2, 3 up to n and back down, so n x n dots
final_answer.spoken: a tilted square grid shows it

maths_rules: 3 x 3 = 9 dots in a grid of 3 rows of 3
tilted 3 by 3 grid has slanting rows of 1, 2, 3, 2, 1 dots
an n by n grid tilted has rows 1, 2, ..., n, ..., 2, 1 and n x n dots
turning a picture does not change the number of dots
video_script.design: One grid of dots is drawn, counted in rows, tilted, and counted again along the slanting rows. The same nine dots stay on the board all video.

<bookmark mark='sums'/>One plus two plus one is four. One up to three and back is nine.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>These totals are square numbers. Can you find a picture that shows why?

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Rows that climb and fall in a tilted square grid add up to a square number. That is why every up and down sum is a square number.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks a diamond is not a square, so its dots cannot make a square number.
<bookmark mark='back'/>Turn the diamond back, and the same dots sit in a square again.
<bookmark mark='strike'/>Turning a picture changes how it looks, but it never changes how many dots there are.
